project.label: SecretAgent — embeddable agent runtime and its desktop agent
project.purpose: Extract the best part of four agent harnesses (DeepSeek Harness, Prime Agent, Claude Code, Onyx) into a portable C library for an embeddable agent, and the desktop agent that runs it.

atlas-root.label: Embeddable agent runtime and its desktop agent
atlas-root.description: A synthesis of the best parts of four symlink'd agent harnesses, rebuilt as a portable C library (embeddable in any host language/environment) plus the desktop agent that runs it, with WaveDB as the durable floor. What each donor contributes (design rationale in docs/chat.json): DeepSeek Harness (./deepseek-harness) — the spine: log-is-source-of-truth, the loop, the guarded tool pipeline; Prime Agent (./prime-agent) — the shape: scoped frames, encapsulation, memory hierarchy, /refine; Claude Code (./claude-code-source-code) — the escalation pattern (plan → ask → act); Onyx (./onyx) — the persona: its response instructions distilled into the loadable persona text (the 'hammer' spec, chat.json message 4148) — and WaveDB (pre-existing, done) as the substrate. All work must stay cross-platform (Linux and Windows green) and embeddable; portability is an invariant of every record, not a separate slice. Layer traceability: L0 WaveDB substrate (done), L1 unified log/tree, L2 frame/scope + surface API, L3 the loop, L4 tool pipeline + interpreter-as-a-tool, L5 persona + escalation as loadable text. The extracted liboffs actor runtime (actor, mailbox, scheduler, refcounter, platform shims) and its 58 passing tests are the existing foundation.
atlas-root.completionRoute: Four delivered slices with independent review per record: the runtime executes agent code without blocking, sessions survive restarts replayably, sessions subdivide into an accountable agent tree, and the desktop agent drives real work on top of the library. Cross-platform builds and the full gtest suite stay green at every completion.

execute-agent-code-without-blocking.label: Execute agent code without blocking the runtime
execute-agent-code-without-blocking.description:
An actor frame can execute Python in a live CPython subinterpreter while the actor keeps processing messages: EXECUTE is enqueued to the interpreter thread, log/status messages stream out to the parent live, and a RESULT returns corr-matched when the cell finishes. The interpreter is a bound tool, never the substrate; a swappable backend keeps C extensions that cannot live in a subinterpreter usable via a subprocess path. This is L4's execution verb on the L3 runtime spine. If cut, the runtime routes and persists but never computes — agents cannot close the loop on their own output. MILESTONE (pyrt layer delivered): non-blocking subinterpreter EXECUTE with live
 log/status streaming, corr-matched RESULT, lazy boot, pool cap, idle eviction,
 cooperative interrupt (forced paths inert per pinned 3.12.13 verification),
 subprocess fallback with fd discipline. Remaining for slice completion:
 Windows build (PCBuild ExternalProject branch), streaming-per-cell attribution (LOG/STATus payloads carry no corr today), review records per lifecycle.

completionEvidence: A running actor answers interrupt/control messages while a slow Python cell executes on its subinterpreter thread (cooperative: honored at cell boundaries only; a running cell is not preemptible on the pinned 3.12 chain)
Python code posts log/status messages whose bytes are attributed per cell and appear live before completion
A RESULT message returns with a correlation id matching the EXECUTE request
Execution backend is swappable (subinterpreter primary, subprocess fallback)

remember-session-across-restarts.label: Survive restarts with a replayable session log
remember-session-across-restarts.description: Sessions live as WaveDB subtrees: events at sessions/<sid>/events/<seq>, lineage at meta/parent, depth at meta/depth. Every state mutation is both a store write and a logged event (one atomic batch), so the log is the single source of truth and views (message history, tree) are projections. RECUT (2026-09-29): the frame-tree slice builds state directly on WaveDB (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-frame-tree-model-loop-design.md), so this slice is now the kill-and-replay VERIFICATION, not a build: rebuild with a fresh boot, reverse-scan seq restore, replay-derived context, recovery from non-compacted WAL. Sessions live as WaveDB subtrees: events at sessions/<sid>/events/<seq>, lineage at meta/parent, depth at meta/depth. Verified WaveDB facts that shape the verification (docs/wavedb-exploration.md): batch atomicity spans subtrees as one WAL_BATCH/txn (capped by wal_config.max_file_size, 128 KB default); scan resume is seek-based half-open; durability at ack is a wal_sync_mode choice; seq keys zero-padded; lineage = graph SPO/POS per-hop scans; one WaveDB per process (frames = subtrees of the single root database); no clone/snapshot needed (fork = lineage pointer + new subtree). KILL-AND-RESUME EVIDENCE (2026-09-30): the proof test exists and runs — TestLoop.TestRestartReplayRestoresSeqAndContext (test/test_loop.cpp) writes a session to a scratch-disk WaveDB (msg.append + ctx remember), closes the store, reopens it, and resumes the SAME sid with frame_resume: birth record is required loudly before any write, recall resolves the remembered value across the restart, the replayed msg.append and ctx snapshot reach the next turn's derived context through the injected model vtable, and a post-resume append lands at a seq strictly past every pre-restart event (asserted through a third session's view due to the open documented WaveDB defect below). Open finding from the verification, on the record: in WaveDB CONCURRENT mode a write committed after a reopen is durable (a fresh session sees and replays it) but INVISIBLE to the same session's own scans and point-gets — the test documents and works around it with a third-session assertion. Suite state: 116 ctest green (ON and ASan under setarch -R), 76 on the OFF build, valgrind clean on the frame/loop/pyrt binaries. FRAME-ORCHESTRATION PROOF (2026-10-01, commits 40541fc..9cd85ca — pool-carried frame actors + frame_start 22085ac; store actor serializing writes and reads with no locks 0de24d6; store scans honoring the requested limit 2f5e552; turn loop dissolved into scheduled turn-step continuations 7a3ab17; resume guard after cfg parse 76a7cc3; http_client deferred teardown 8fb0fb0; async http model submit f6946b7; deferred destroy across a pending async submit ef459dd; spawn admits and starts, parents resume on child report events f43f73b; child failure fails loud, one report per child 534ae3d; no-lock grep scoped to the frame-engine files 9cd85ca): the replay proof now holds under the event-driven engine — a resumed frame's engine re-runs off its persistent log through the store actor's serialized reads (the async engine driving the same loop is proven by TestLoop.TestAsyncScriptedBackendDrivesTheSameEngine). The store actor is the ONLY serializer of frame state: no platform_mutex/rwlock/barrier/sem anywhere in the frame-engine files (frame.c / frame_internal.h / loop.c / frame_messages.h / frame.h — the standing grep is clean; src/Frame/model.c's install-once loop guard and completion-pair record mutexes are the recorded off-dispatch exception); every cross-frame state effect is ONE atomic WaveDB batch behind the store actor and seq counters are pre-allocated in each frame's own actor. Valgrind breadth on the final build (symbol-keeping --strip-debug copy, verified executing, raised store waits SA_FRAME_STORE_WAIT_MS=600000 / SA_LOOP_STORE_WAIT_MS=300000) over TestFrame/TestStore/TestFrameTree/TestLoop/TestModelDecode: 38 tests, 0 errors, definitely-lost 0; the scratch-disk restart test itself is excluded (pathologically slow under valgrind emulation, documented on S006) and the python-cell suites' leak proof is ASan over the whole 153-test suite. The opt-in live gate PASSED riding the pump against local Ollama (gemma4:latest, 67.6 s) — it remains endpoint-dependent: the same endpoint degraded earlier that day answered system-only prompts finish_reason:"load", and the gate records such captures honestly instead of passing on them. subdivide-session-into-accountable-agent.label: Subdivide sessions into an accountable agent tree
subdivide-session-into-accountable-agent.description: RECUT (2026-09-29): the frame-tree slice (drive-model-driven-frame-tree) built spawn/report/admission semantics; this slice is now the ACCOUNTABILITY VERIFICATION at tree scale (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-frame-tree-model-loop-design.md): parent context grows by exactly one report event per child regardless of child work volume; the frame tree derives reconstructably from lineage pointers; no #819-style scoping blind spot (children see inherited ctx only via the resolve walk, never local); compaction stays per-frame. VERIFICATION RESULT (2026-10-01, folded into the frame-orchestration slice's acceptance, commits 40541fc..9cd85ca): the accountability invariants hold at tree scale with the store actor as the ONLY serializer of frame state — no platform lock anywhere in the frame-engine files (frame.c / frame_internal.h / loop.c / frame_messages.h / frame.h; src/Frame/model.c's off-dispatch mutexes are the recorded exception), one atomic WaveDB batch per cross-frame effect, seq counters pre-allocated in each frame's own actor. One report per child under concurrent scheduling: TestFrameTree.TestPooledTreeKeepsOneReportPerChildWithContiguousSeq proves a contiguous seq chain over N spawned children's bound reports WITHOUT any lock — WaveDB's writes and reads serialize behind the root's store actor. The tree derives reconstructably from lineage pointers (TestFrame.TestReportBindsOneEventIntoParent, TestFrame.TestReportBindIsOneCrossSubtreeBatch). #819's scoping blind spot demonstrably absent — children resolve inherited ctx only via the resolve walk. Child failure fails loud: a control event lands in the child's log, ONE failure report is bound into the parent, the parent resumes and its derive shows the failure (TestLoop.TestChildTurnLimitFailsIntoTheParent, TestFrameTree.TestPooledChildFailureResumesParentWithTheFailure; TestFrameTree.TestPooledParentSpawnsChildAndResumesOnReport proves spawn → inline yield → resume-on-report → completion with no thread waiting on a child). run-agent-as-desktop.label: Run the agent from the desktop
run-agent-as-desktop.description: A desktop/CLI client embeds the C library and drives real agent sessions end to end: frames run, code executes, sessions persist and subdivide, and results come back. Persona and escalation load as text modules (plan → ask → act) shaping the loop — the assistant's behavior is text, versionable and checkable, not compiled in. Provenance: the persona text is distilled from the Onyx harness's response instructions (./onyx; the 'hammer' persona spec in docs/chat.json message 4148), and the escalation gate design is lifted from the Claude Code source (./claude-code-source-code). This is L3+L5 and the moment the runtime becomes a product anyone can drive. If cut, the library exists but nothing runs it: there is no desktop agent.

drive-model-driven-frame-tree.label: Drive a model-driven frame tree on WaveDB
drive-model-driven-frame-tree.description: The turn loop, one OpenAI-compatible model client (single execute tool, PA-verified single-tool RLM shape), the four bridge verbs as actor behaviors (remember/recall/spawn/report) — in-process, no wire protocol — admission-only spawn/report, frame state as WaveDB subtrees of one root database per process, one atomic root batch per effect (event + state + lineage triples). Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-frame-tree-model-loop-design.md. Absorbs the build that S003/S004 would have front-loaded; S004's accountability invariants and S003's replay proof verify this work rather than building it. MILESTONE (2026-09-30, turn loop + model client + demo): the model-driven round trip runs end to end — frame store on WaveDB subtrees, turn loop (src/Frame/loop.c: derive-from-events per turn, model call, tool path to a real pyrt cell, content path, loud control events), OpenAI-compatible client (src/Frame/model.c, single execute tool, both tool_call argument shapes), http transport on the ported liboffs streams stack (2026-09-30 slice: deps/poll-dancer pinned a05b9e1 + http-parser ec8b5ee6 + pcre2 for Windows; the express-like server core + auth_middleware + bcrypt ported byte-except-includes into src/Streams and loopback-proven by TestStreamsServer; the SYNC src/Net/http client RETIRED - model completions now ride a NEW async http client on the poll-dancer loop thread behind SA_ENABLE_STREAMS, submit-copies-arguments, at-most-one completion, a refcounted completion record in model.c; the Task-8 framing hardening re-pinned test-for-test async; configs: 135 ON/ASan, 62 OFF; Windows/IOCP paths compile-gated, verification pending a Windows environment), four bridge verbs. Evidence: demo CLI (tools/frame-demo, one top frame on a real scratch-disk WaveDB against local Ollama) — commit 5d7aedf + smoke; scripted-loop tests without network — TestLoop suite injects the model vtable (cell-run-and-report, steering reorder between turns, loud turn-limit cap); restart/replay proof — TestLoop.TestRestartReplayRestoresSeqAndContext (scratch-disk db, close, reopen, frame_resume: recall across the restart, replayed msg.append + ctx reach the next derive, seq continues strictly past pre-restart events); opt-in live integration gate — TestLiveLoop.TestLiveOllamaRememberAndReportWave (registered unconditionally, GTEST_SKIP unless SA_TEST_OLLAMA_URL is set). Follow-up live-gate fixes (all on master): model completion timeout is a frame-config seam (frame_config_t.model_timeout_ms, 0 = the 30 s built-in default; the live gate carries 180 s) and transport failures surface the http layer's reason instead of a bare "(no body)" - commit 69ae696; fresh interpreters bind the injected actor module so a bare actor.remember works without an import - 4be64ff; the python bridge speaks python values (json.dumps/loads at the store boundary, so remember('word', 'wave') round trips) - e336572; an empty model stop lands on the audit trail as a control "empty-turn" event instead of vanishing - cbbad1d; the live gate reruns the scenario on fresh frames (up to three attempts: the plan's literal goal, then a sharper instruction) with [  AUDIT  ] dumps so a narrating stop diagnoses itself - 17d969a. Residual model-side behavior (kept, not fixed): a reasoning model may narrate and stop instead of calling the tool - the reasoning then surfaces as the assistant text (model.c decodes a non-empty reasoning field as the turn's content when content is empty), the stop lands as an audit event, and the gate's fresh-frame reruns absorb the nondeterminism.

refine-continual-harness.label: Refine: supplemental state as a WaveDB subtree, evidence-backed lessons, append-only rollback
refine-continual-harness.description:
The continual-harness /refine slice (Prime Agent's refinement port, spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-01-refine-design.md, the parity-feature-matrix section 3/6 sketch): supplemental state is a WaveDB SUBTREE, never a side file. Schema: session-local by default at sessions/<sid>/harness/… (harness/log/<seq> the AUTHORITATIVE append-only records, harness/entry/<kind>/<id> the folded current-entry materialization, harness/meta/fingerprint + harness/meta/digest), with root-level harness/… as the shared opt-in scope (--refine-global): shared is READ-ONLY CONTEXT during a local refinement and cross-scope edits refuse loud (refinement.ts:380-407's merge discipline). Commit rule: every refinement write is ONE atomic store batch through the frame's store actor (FRM_STORE_SCAN reviews, FRM_STORE_BATCH commits, the entry withdrawal is a real WaveDB type-1 DELETE op on the materialized entry) — no new actor, no new thread, NO lock anywhere: the store actor remains the only serializer (the frame-tree slice's store-actor milestone is exactly the property this slice rides). History is APPEND-ONLY (the DB-as-log: the log alone is truth, entries/digests fold from it): a rollback is a NEW record carrying the rollbackOf link and the original's inverse edits — the original record stays byte-identical after; nothing in the log is ever mutated or deleted. The evidence gate (the spec §4 recorded OURS-divergence): every edit requires evidence first..last event seqs — an edit without evidence refuses ("edit without evidence"), and a proposal with zero valid edits commits NOTHING (the loud no-op; rc==1 is a defined PASS shape). PA's reviewer is trusted to ground itself; ours FAILS LOUD because the owner's shape is small, EVIDENCE-BACKED writes the store can prove. Fingerprint gate ports: refine-time fingerprint gate (agent-session.ts:7238-7245's commit-only-when-fingerprint-changed, ported so a second refine with no fold change commits no record) and the FNV-1a-64 fingerprint over the canonical fold material (equal folds give equal fingerprints, version-only bookkeeping excluded, refinement.ts:777-843; the digest render is capped refinement.ts:20-22). The review call is never a tool: refine never appears in any model surface — the review completion carries tools as JSON null (model.c's single omission shape), and base_system_prompt is refused at every action. PARITY (spec §8, citations inline in each test): rows 1-4 the record lifecycle with version guards — TestCreateUpdateDeleteLifecycleAppliesPerKind, TestCreateDerivesSlugIdAndDefaults (the slug port), TestStaleTargetRejectedOnVersionMismatch, TestSequentialEditsToSameEntryApply, TestCreateOnExistingUpdateAndDeleteOnMissingRefuse; row 5 the evidence gate + no-op rule — TestEditWithoutEvidenceRefusedAndZeroEditsAreNoop; row 6 the skill contract — TestSkillContractCarriesPythonReferenceAndArguments; row 7 base_system_prompt refused — TestBaseSystemPromptIdRefusedEveryAction; row 8 fingerprint stability — TestCanonicalViewsRefuseNullFold, TestFingerprintStableForEqualFold, TestFingerprintDiffersOnContentAndVersion, TestFingerprintSaltedVersionString; row 9 digest bounds — TestDigestRenderBounded; rows 10-12 rollback — TestRollbackComposesTheInverseFromTheRecord, TestRollbackMissingTargetRefused, TestRollbackAfterLaterEditRejectsStaleInverse; row 13 the fingerprint gate — TestRepeatedRefineWithNoChangeCommitsNothing; row 14 the over-budget batch refuses — TestRefineBatchOverBudgetRefusesNothingCommitted; row 15 the pooled-store refusal — TestRefinesOnPooledStoreRefuseLoud; row 16 the trajectory-scan caps — TestTrajectoryScanNewestCapHolds, TestReviewTrajectoryTailSliceDropsWholeOldestRecords; row 17 the scopes — TestSharedScopeSeparateAndReadOnlyFromLocal, TestLocalRefineRendersSeededSharedContext; row 18 the no-tools review call — TestRequestBodyOmitsToolsOnJsonNull, TestReviewCallPassesJsonNullTools; row 19 malformed log records skipped loud — TestFoldParsesRollbackEvidenceShape, TestFoldRefusesMalformedRollbackEvidence; the supporting store/decode/runit round trips riding the same gates — TestSyncScanReturnsNewestAscendingAsJointArray, TestProposalDecodeCapsAndFences, TestRefineRunCommitsOneAtomicBatch, TestRefineRunNoopCommitsNothing; row 20 THE LIVE GATE (opt-in, outcome-independent assertions only) — TestRefineLiveRefineAgainstRealModel. EVIDENCE: 33 committed tests in test/test_refine.cpp, full suite green (189/189 debug + ASan under setarch -R; refine tests registered under the WDB gate, absent from the OFF build), valgrind clean over TestRefine.*, the no-locks grep clean over src/Frame (model.c's recorded exceptions unchanged), and the live gate's real-model run (the outcome-independent invariant set — folded fingerprint + digest exist and the stored meta matches the recomputed fold, or the loud no-op):
